title: The Seeds (Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm female vocal 100bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling intimate garden seeds wisdom Perth Zimbabwe family seasons
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The seeds are patience in the smallest possible form
A piece of information waiting for the warmth
You put them in the ground and you water them and wait
And the seeds remind you that the best things are not late
They're just on their own schedule — and that schedule is their own

[Pre-Chorus]
I've been planting seeds in this garden since before my children were grown
And the garden gives them back to me in every season's tone

[Chorus]
The seeds, the seeds
Small things with large intentions and particular needs
The seeds, the seeds
They know the season before the season knows itself
The seeds know more about the future than the shelf
The gardens still growing

[Verse 2]
Some seeds take one season, some seeds take three years
Some seeds need a fire before the casing clears
The banksia needs a bushfire before it will open
And I have always found that image worth the token

[Bridge]
I planted rosemary near the path because the scent
Is the same as the rosemary in the garden where I spent
My girlhood in Zimbabwe — and when I walk past now
The garden takes me back across the years and shows me how

[Outro]
The seeds know everything they need to be… the garden knows…
The gardens still growing
